episodes.203672: After a brief, but very welcome period of drier weather, showers and thunderstorms returned to the area on July 25th as moisture increased ahead of a cold front. Initially, most of the activity was confined to northern West Virginia and parts of southeast Ohio during the day, with a lull in precipitation overnight. Scattered showers and storms then sprouted up across the area on the 26th, where some activity even continued into the night. The next day began with more scattered showers and storms before a more robust line of thunderstorms developed along an outflow boundary that afternoon and evening. After an overnight reprieve, scattered activity redeveloped across southern West Virginia, northeast Kentucky, and southwest Virginia on the 28th. That evening, a line of thunderstorms traversed southeast Ohio and then began to fall apart after pushing east of the Ohio River. This brought the end to the active weather period for a few days across West Virginia.||Daily occurrences of severe weather and flash flooding took place across the state in the midst of this event. Flash flooding occurred in Harrison County on the 25th after storms deposited two to three inches of rain in the southwestern part of the county. Additional instances of flooding also materialized in Wood County on the 28th following rounds of heavy rain over a couple of days. The main impacts from this multiple day stretch of active weather was observed within downed trees and power lines across the area due to stronger wind gusts embedded within thunderstorms.
episodes.203748: An additional short-wave trough moving through the region along with moist unstable airmass contributed to several days of late afternoon to early evening thunderstorms.
episodes.203890: A wet period at the end of the July resulted in saturated soils and increased runoff, allowing isolated river flooding along the upper Big Sioux River Basin. Minor to very localized moderate river flooding was observed.
episodes.203924: A slow moving cold front combined with a highly unstable atmosphere along with tropical moisture to produce slow moving thunderstorms with heavy rainfall. Some of these storms trained over the same areas, resulting in scattered instances of flash flooding. Total rainfall amounts in areas with flash flooding averaged two to four inches.
episodes.203987: A hot and humid air mass combined with orographical lift to produce a severe thunderstorm in Surry County of northwest North Carolina. Damaging wind gusts from this storm blew down one tree and one power line.
episodes.204042: A combination of limited moisture and weak forcing from shortwave energy and diurnal heating resulted in isolated high based showers and thunderstorms.
episodes.204068: A shortwave rotating around the eastern side of a mid level ridge provided a lifting mechanism for widespread thunderstorms. CAPE values around 2000 J/kg was sufficient enough to produce several strong storms, but a lack of bulk shear kept all but one storm below severe limits.
episodes.204109: A rear east to west moving severe thunderstorm produced large hail along Colorado High 94 in southwest Lincoln County. The largest stones measured were 2.75 inches.
episodes.204151: In the afternoon of the 29th, scattered storms moved to the northeast across eastern Colorado. Hail up to one inch was reported near Vernon.
episodes.204153: In the afternoon of the 29th, scattered storms moved to the northeast across eastern Colorado into northwestern Kansas. Winds near Atwood caused tree damage, and hail up to 0.8 inches were measured.
episodes.204156: During the evening and overnight hours of the 29th, clusters of storms formed in northwestern Kansas before entering southwestern Nebraska. These storms filled into a broken line, and began training over a portion of southern Red Willow county, on the state line. An estimated 6 inches of running water was seen over Nebraska road 89. Also, hail up to pennies was reported.
episodes.204324: Severe thunderstorms moved east through southern McCone county.
episodes.204447: Heavy rainfall led to minor flash flooding on the southside of Pueblo and just east of Pueblo Reservoir.
episodes.204562: Ahead of a cold front approaching from the north, a west to east bowing line of convection dropped south through central Kentucky. A few isolated reports of tree damage were reported out of Ohio County.
episodes.204832: Two fair-weather waterspouts were photographed off of Surf City, NC.
episodes.204908: Scattered thunderstorms developed across southwest Georgia in a summertime airmass. One storm produced large hail in Grady county.
episodes.204933: In the pre-sunrise hours of July 29th, an MCS dove south into west-central Illinois. As it passed, the storm caused isolated wind damage in Quincy before moving off.
episodes.204936: In the pre-sunrise hours of July 29th, an MCS dove south into northeast Missouri. As it passed, the storm caused wind damage in Palmyra before moving off.
episodes.204938: During the late afternoon of July 29th, discrete convection developed in eastern Missouri. Thunderstorms were forecast to be disorganized with severe winds possible. The only location in Missouri to see severe winds that afternoon was in eastern Jefferson County.
episodes.204963: Diurnally enhanced storms produced locally heavy rainfall given high precipitable water (near 2 inches) across the area and added upper-level lift with an upper-level wave moving east to west across the FL peninsula. Extreme heat warning and a heat advisory were in effect given high heat index values, with also supported very high surface instability that fed into stronger storms.
episodes.205121: A moist and unstable summer airmass led to the development of scattered afternoon thunderstorms, a few of which were strong to severe.
episodes.205123: A moist and unstable summer airmass led to the development of scattered afternoon thunderstorms, a few of which were strong to severe.
episodes.205221: Heavy rainfall across central and west central Arkansas lead to isolated flash flooding.
episodes.205272: A persistent troughing pattern brought in good instability and shear to produce severe thunderstorms across the region over the 3 day time frame with strong winds as the primary hazard. There was also isolated large hail. Anomalously high moisture content and slower moving storms brought localized flooding. A thunderstorm produced heavy rainfall and caused flooding in Havre and in Clear Creek on the 27th. The Havre airport reported 1.72 inches in about 45 minutes, with other reports in town estimated 2.5 of rain quickly. There were also flooding along Highway 69 & 55 in Jefferson County on the 29th.
episodes.205283: An upper level ridge of high pressure in place across the Four State Region on July 29th began to weaken slightly as a westward advancing inverted trough aloft drifted into portions of the Lower Mississippi Valley and Northeast Louisiana. Strong heating with temperatures climbing into the upper 90s to near 100 degrees coupled with rich low level moisture created a very unstable environment, resulting in the development of scattered showers and thunderstorms across much of this area during the afternoon of the 29th. Some of these storms became severe, causing multiple downbursts with strong, damaging winds which downed numerous trees and power lines across Ouachita Parish before diminishing by early evening.
episodes.205411: A line of thunderstorms developed over western MN and progressed eastward during the evening of July 28th, 2025. As this line of storms reached eastern MN, storm intensity increased, producing 60 to 70 mph damaging wind gusts across the Twin Cities metro down to Mankato.||There were numerous reports of trees down and power outages across several areas.  A couple noteworthy gusts were measured by the Scott County Mesonet in Shakopee at 65 mph.  The Owatonna airport AWOS in Steele Co measured 70 mph.
episodes.205474: On July 29th, a well-organized line of severe progressed from South Dakota into Iowa during the very early the morning hours. Severe thunderstorm wind gusts occurred in eastern Iowa with scattered gusts between 70 to 80 MPH. Wind gusts over 40 MPH lasted for 30 minutes in some places. This line of storms was classified as a derecho by the Storm Prediction Center.
episodes.205485: A well-organized line of severe progressed from South Dakota through northern and eastern Iowa and finally into northwest Illinois. during the very early the morning hours of July 29. Severe thunderstorm wind gusts (58+ MPH) occurred in Rock island County well the line of storm rapidly weakening as it moved eastward. This line of storms was classified as a derecho by the Storm Prediction Center.
episodes.205508: Early on July 28, 2025, a mesoscale convective system (MCS) tracking south across Iowa triggered a brief period of damaging winds in extreme eastern Nebraska and southwestern Iowa. An outflow boundary from the MCS pushed into the region, producing a 58 mph gust at 1:45 AM CST measured by the ASOS in Tekamah, Nebraska. Later, at 2:21 AM CST, law enforcement reported a roof blown off a home in Mondamin, Iowa. As the morning progressed, radar showed the outflow boundary weakening and becoming more diffuse, leading to no additional severe weather reports.||That evening, another round of storms developed along a cold front stretching from north-central Nebraska into southeastern South Dakota, impacting northeast Nebraska. Although most of the storm activity occurred outside the area, one storm clipped northeast Nebraska, where emergency management reported a measured 1-inch hailstone 4 miles southwest of Niobrara, Nebraska, at 7:23 PM CST.
episodes.205514: Storms moving from northeast South Dakota generated strong winds in west-central Minnesota. Heavy rainfall from these and previous storms also resulted in localized flooding.
episodes.205515: Strong thunderstorms traveled from central to northeast South Dakota during the afternoon and evening of July 28th. Hail was measured at 3.5 inches diameter 5 miles north of Cresbard to baseball sized near Chelsea, with damage to vehicles, siding and nearby crops. As the storms continued east, they generated strong winds, with a peak gust of 77 mph recorded by the South Dakota Department of Transportation mesonet station 1 mile north northwest of Summit.
episodes.205748: Thunderstorms developed along a broken line extending from the western Sandhills northeast into far northern Nebraska and south central South Dakota during the early evening hours of July 28th. This activity quickly grew upscale with a solid line of thunderstorms by 6 PM CDT. Storm activity maintained its intensity over far northern Nebraska through 9 PM CDT, before weakening. Thunderstorm wind gusts up to 62 MPH were reported at the Valentine Airport and hail up to 2.5 inches in diameter was reported in Keya Paha County.
episodes.205763: A line of strong thunderstorms developed over southern Indiana in the late afternoon and moved south on the east side of a strong ridge of high pressure aloft. Southwest Indiana was in the midst of a multi-week heat wave, and the extreme heat and humidity provided fuel for the line of storms to continue south with the western end of the line passing from Oakland City to Newburgh in the early evening. A few downbursts within the line produced damaging winds near Oakland City and Otwell.
episodes.205764: A line of strong thunderstorms developed over southern Indiana in the late afternoon and moved south on the east side of a strong ridge of high pressure aloft. Western Kentucky was in the midst of a multi-week heat wave, and the extreme heat and humidity provided fuel for the line of storms to continue southward through much of west Kentucky during the evening. Occasional downbursts resulted in sporadic damaging winds from eastern Daviess county southward into Muhlenberg county, where the storms weakened.
episodes.205765: Southeast Missouri was in the midst of a prolonged heat wave and the extreme heat and humidity supported a cluster of thunderstorms in the late afternoon and early evening. The storms moved southwestward across northwest Wayne County and through Carter County.  Occasional downbursts resulted in sporadic damaging winds from the Clearwater Lake area to Van Buren.
episodes.205831: Afternoon sea breeze convection within easterly flow produces gusty winds over Tampa Bay area waters.
episodes.205845: During the late evening hours on July 28th, a line of intense thunderstorms moved into southeast Minnesota and produced severe wind gusts along with widespread wind damage. Most notably a wind gust of 76 mph was observed at Rochester International Airport along with several other wind gusts over 70 mph across the region. Storms eventually moved south and east into Wisconsin and Iowa as they weakened overnight.
episodes.205847: During the late evening hours on July 28th and into the very early morning hours on the 29th, two distinct lines of intense thunderstorms moved through portions of northeast Iowa. The first of these storms was in its weakening stages producing some sporadic wind damage. The second pushed east out of northern Iowa and grazed Floyd through Fayette counties with severe wind gusts and tree damage. This second line of storms was later classified as a derecho by the Storm Prediction Center.
episodes.205848: During the late evening hours on July 28th and into the very early morning hours on the 29th, a line of weakening thunderstorms crossed the Mississippi River into Wisconsin. Initially, these storms produced widespread wind damage as they crossed the river with multiple gusts to around 60 to 70 mph. However, as they pushed further east into Wisconsin they quickly weakened below severe levels.
episodes.205881: A couple of severe thunderstorm outflow wind gusts were recorded.
episodes.205886: A large cluster of storms moving across Lyman county produced large hail and damaging winds.
episodes.205942: An isolated supercell thunderstorm developed along an outflow boundary in a moderately unstable atmosphere. The storm became severe, briefly producing very strong winds estimated at 100 mph to the southeast of Charlson in McKenzie County. In this area a single wide manufactured home was blown off its cinder block foundation, displaced approximately 50 to 60 feet, and completely destroyed. A livestock trailer was flipped onto its roof, a metal storage container was shifted and tipped onto its side and a large dumpster was blown approximately 100 feet. Nearby several panels of a metal industrial building roof were displaced or blown off, and a camper was tipped on its side. Thereafter, the only other severe report was for one-inch diameter hail to the south of Four Bears Lodge.
episodes.205992: Heat bursts were recorded by SD mesonets with afternoon thunderstorms bringing large hail and damaging winds.
episodes.206031: Scattered thunderstorms and storm clusters developed over upstate South Carolina during the afternoon. One of the storms produced brief damaging wind gusts in Spartanburg County.
episodes.206049: A large upper high over the lower Mississippi Valley setup a deep southeast flow off the Gulf bringing above average moisture into far west Texas.  Very heavy rain occurred for several hours and resulted in flash flooding over parts of Hudspeth and far northeastern El Paso counties.
episodes.206050: An upper high over the lower Mississippi Valley brought a deep southeast flow of moisture directly over New Mexico which resulted in severe thunderstorm winds, heavy rain and numerous reports of flash flooding around Luna, Sierra and Otero counties.
episodes.206104: A cold front moved across Wyoming and brought severe thunderstorms to central portions of the state. The main impact from the storms was large hailin Johnson, Hot Springs, Natrona and Fremont Counties. The largest hail was ping pong ball sized hail in Johnson County to the south of Buffalo. The Natrona County airport near Casper had around a 10 minute period of high wind, with gusts as high as 66 mph.
episodes.206184: Two distinct supercell clusters developed across central South Dakota during the late afternoon of July 28 within a highly unstable environment (MUCAPE up to 5000 J/kg) ahead of an eastward advancing surface front. The southern supercell cluster produced three tornadoes across Gregory County, the strongest of which was rated EF2. ||Scattered severe wind gusts were reported across southeast South Dakota as the thunderstorms moved east before the two clusters merged near and south of Sioux Falls. Aided by increasing deep layer shear from the north, a linear structure rapidly developed with a derecho racing eastward into northwest Iowa. Winds gusted from 80 to 100 mph along the derecho's path with widespread tree and structural damage across the area. In addition, three embedded short-lived tornadoes were documented within the line of thunderstorms.

episodes.206200: Scattered strong to severe thunderstorms developed across southeast Louisiana and southern Mississippi on July 29, 2025, along a weak boundary. In Pearl River County, MS, numerous trees were snapped or uprooted near Caesar, with a house losing shingles, an outbuilding destroyed, and several large pecan trees downed. Additional damage was reported in Hammond, LA, where thunderstorm winds downed a tree along Old Covington Highway. Over the waters, the SHBL1 station on Lake Borgne measured a wind gust of 51 mph.

episodes.206228: A large cluster of thunderstorms developed just inland of the southeast South Carolina coast in the afternoon hours. These thunderstorms impacted Beaufort County and Colleton County with gusty winds and frequent lightning.
episodes.206238: Thunderstorms erupted within a very moist and unstable environment across central South Dakota during the afternoon of July 29 in response to an approaching upper level short-wave from Colorado. These thunderstorms quickly grew upscale into a line, producing 55 to 75 mph wind gusts across southeast South Dakota, resulting in isolated tree damage. In addition, prolonged heavy rain resulted in some localized flash flooding across northwest Iowa.
episodes.206299: A line of thunderstorms developed over western MN and progressed east-southeast during the evening of July 28th, 2025. As this line of storms reached western WI, the intensity remained consistent across the region, producing 60 to 70 mph damaging wind gusts across an area extending from St. Croix to Pepin Counties, then eastward to Chippewa and Eau Claire Counties. ||There were numerous reports of trees down and power outages across several areas. Although measured gusts in Pierce Co and Chippewa Counties were between 60 to 65 mph, the degree of damage that occurred in New Richmond (St. Croix) indicated an isolated swath of wind gusts just over 70 mph.
episodes.206392: A few thunderstorms impacted heavily poplulated areas of eastern Montana, producing localized flooding, gusts up to 70 mph, and hail up to 2 inches in diameter.
episodes.206394: A few strong thunderstorms occurred across southern Montana, producing gusts up to 74 mph and hail up to 2 inches in diameter.
episodes.206467: Isolated thunderstorm activity during the late afternoon and evening hours produced a local report of a funnel cloud in central Oregon.
episodes.206762: A derecho moved across northern Iowa, resulting in a swath of wind damage with gusts of 60 to 80 mph reported, along with two tornadoes that occurred along the leading edge of the line of storms. The line of storms developed with an embedded shortwave that rode over a larger upper level ridge. That ridge allowed for hot and humid conditions across the area with temperatures in the upper 80s to low 90s and dewpoints in the 70s, resulting in heat indicies well over 100. This made for a deeply unstable airmass with over 5000 J/kg of MLCAPE and the line of storms rode the CAPE gradient across northern Iowa overnight. With 30-35 kts of 0-6 km shear, convection was able to maintain strength, and 0-3 km shear near 25 kts orthognal to the line was able to provide just enough of a tornadic set up. The line of storms reach western portions of the area by around 11 pm local time and finally exited east just after 2 am local time. Widespread tree damage and power outages were reported with this line of storms.
